clue.text: Horse has elephant's disorder, poor nag

parts.note: must (or musth) is the frenzied state of a male elephant in the rutting season

indicators.note: something in a poor state is in bad shape, so the word after it is knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A horse suffers from an elephant's ailment, the poor old nag.
explanation.walkthrough: MUST is a rare word: a bull elephant's seasonal frenzy, also spelt musth. Nag looks like the definition of a horse, but it is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustang is a wild or half-wild horse of the American plains, descended from Spanish stock.

clue.text: Eskimo dogs (only the birches giving tongue?)

parts.note: surface reading: in the Arctic woods only the trees make a sound
setter's reading: barking; these sled dogs are mute and seldom bark, so the only bark is on the birch trees

explanation.walkthrough: Giving tongue is a hunting term for hounds barking. The breed is famously quiet, and its name ends in mutes; birches have bark of the other kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alaskan malamute is a powerful sledge dog bred by the Inuit, once commonly called Eskimo.

clue.text: Garment for one sort of square

parts.note: meant for only one person, as a single room
a T-square is a draughtsman's ruler

explanation.surface: Clothing intended for a certain kind of square person.
explanation.walkthrough: Square seems to describe a person, but the T-square is a drawing tool shaped like the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless vest worn as underwear or by athletes, so it is an item of clothing.

clue.text: Court case about theologian, one with a drug problem

indicators.note: about means around, so the words for court case surround what follows

parts.note: an action is a lawsuit
DD is Doctor of Divinity
the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A lawsuit about a churchman, one of the parties a drug user.
explanation.walkthrough: One reads as a person, but it supplies the numeral I, which joins the theologian's letters inside ACTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Addiction is dependence on a substance, which is what a drug problem amounts to.

clue.text: Swallow tobacco on rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the word for tobacco runs backwards

parts.note: a plug is a cake of pressed tobacco for chewing

explanation.surface: Taking a mouthful of tobacco on getting up.
explanation.walkthrough: Swallow could be the bird, but it is the verb. A plug of tobacco is the chewing kind.
explanation.definitionFit: To gulp is to swallow quickly in large mouthfuls, so the verb and the definition are synonyms.

clue.text: Part of Greater London Transport?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a borough in the east of the capital
second meaning: a horse-drawn carriage for hire, the origin of the licensed taxi

explanation.surface: It reads as a query about a section of the capital's public transport network.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface runs the two meanings together as London Transport, the old name of the city's bus and Underground authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackney is a London borough, and a hackney carriage is the legal term for a cab plying for hire.

clue.text: Death of an Admiral — a novel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the end of Lord Howard of Effingham, who led the English fleet against the Armada
second meaning: E. M. Forster's 1910 novel about the Schlegel sisters

explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, the title is the end of a man named Howard; the Admiral is Lord Howard, commander against the Spanish Armada in 1588.
explanation.definitionFit: Forster's novel takes its title from a country house, and the phrase also reads as the demise of one Howard.

clue.text: Some give welcome to a space-traveller

indicators.note: some means a portion of, so only part of the following words is used

parts.note: the letters run across the second and third words

explanation.surface: Some people greet a visitor from outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: Some looks like the subject of give, people greeting an alien, but it only marks the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet is an icy body that travels through the solar system, so it is a space-traveller.

clue.text: A time for resolution, not without honour

definitions.text: A time for resolution, not without honour

parts.note: surface reading: a moment for firm decision, when the season of making pledges comes round
setter's reading: the occasion when the British honours list is published, echoing the saying about a prophet

explanation.surface: A moment of decisive resolve, which brings its own distinction.
explanation.walkthrough: Not without honour echoes 'a prophet is not without honour, save in his own country'. Britain publishes a New Year Honours list of knighthoods and medals.
explanation.definitionFit: People make resolutions as the calendar turns over, and the British honours list is announced then too.

clue.text: Bowls for the county

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket, gets a batsman out with a yorker, a ball pitched at the feet
second meaning: the abbreviation for Yorkshire, the largest English county

explanation.surface: Someone bowls for their county side, as in county cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: A yorker is a cricket delivery aimed at the batsman's toes; to york someone is to dismiss them with one.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket uses the verb for bowling a batsman with a yorker, and the short form names Yorkshire.

clue.text: Showing signs of age as coat might be

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a face marked with wrinkles
second meaning: a garment with an inner layer of fabric sewn in

explanation.surface: Something showing its years, as an old coat might.
explanation.definitionFit: An ageing face is furrowed with wrinkles, and a coat often has a silk or fleece layer inside.

clue.text: It reduces production of seeds at Wimbledon

definitions.text: It reduces production of seeds at Wimbledon

parts.words: It reduces production of seeds at Wimbledon
parts.note: surface reading: something that knocks the top-ranked players out of the tennis championship
setter's reading: grass, which produces seed, cut short on the courts by a garden machine

explanation.surface: Something cuts down the number of seeded players at the tennis championship.
explanation.walkthrough: Seeds at Wimbledon are top-ranked players, but here they are grass seed; the grass courts must be kept trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: The machine cuts grass, the plant that produces seeds, and Wimbledon is played on grass courts.

clue.text: Spitefulness of married woman

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for married
a woman's name

explanation.surface: A wife's spite, as if from a gossip column.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the wish to harm someone, which is what spitefulness amounts to.

clue.text: Hog's for horses

definitions.note: possessive standing for the noun it implies: a hog's feet
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pig's feet, as sold by a butcher
second meaning: horses bred and raced at a trotting gait

explanation.surface: Something belonging to a pig is meant for horses.
explanation.walkthrough: Hog's leaves its noun unsaid: what a hog has that is also a name for horses is its feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig's feet are cooked and sold as trotters, and harness-racing horses are also called trotters.

clue.text: Mood of the commander

parts.note: surface reading: the officer's temper today
setter's reading: a grammatical mood, the verb form used for giving orders

explanation.surface: The officer in charge is in a certain frame of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: In grammar, a mood is a verb form; the one used for orders, as in 'Halt!', is what a commander uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar's imperative mood expresses commands, so it is the verb form an officer issuing orders uses.

clue.text: All the composer required

parts.note: surface reading: everything the composer asked for
setter's reading: the Italian marking a composer writes in a score when every player is to join in

explanation.surface: Everything a composer needed for a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Scores use Italian directions; this one tells the whole orchestra to play together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical direction means everyone plays, so it is literally the word for all.

clue.text: Doctor carries animal to land, slaughtered

indicators.note: a carrier holds its load, so the doctor's letters hold what follows

parts.note: MD is Doctor of Medicine
a donkey
a unit of land area

explanation.surface: A vet takes a beast off to a field, where it is killed.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor looks like a verb meaning to falsify, but it is the noun; MD stands for Doctor of Medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: To be massacred is to be killed brutally and indiscriminately, which is what slaughtered means.

clue.text: Companion is at sea, possibly, holding up business

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the word for business runs backwards
holding means keeping something inside, so the reworked letters wrap around what follows
possibly means this is only one way the words could go, so their letters may be reordered

parts.note: the three words taken letter by letter
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A partner at sea delays a commercial venture.
explanation.walkthrough: At sea hints at the jumble but is fodder too; holding up reads as delaying but is two signals.
explanation.definitionFit: An associate is a partner or colleague, someone who keeps company with another as a companion.

clue.text: Urge to go into action, though dispirited

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it, so the word for urge sits within the other

parts.note: a deed is an act
to urge is to press someone

explanation.surface: Someone feels the urge to act although low in spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Being depressed means feeling low and gloomy, the same state as being disheartened or downcast.

clue.text: Age Maud had, not reached

parts.note: surface reading: some age a woman called Maud never got to
setter's reading: the heroine of Tennyson's poem, of whom he writes that she is not yet this age

explanation.surface: A woman named Maud, and an age she had not yet arrived at.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's poem Maud says of its heroine 'Maud is not seventeen, But she is tall and stately'.
explanation.definitionFit: The number is an age, the one Tennyson's heroine is said in the poem not yet to have reached.

clue.text: Not evil but wild and fierce

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters before it run loose into a new order

parts.note: the two words taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A creature that is not wicked, merely untamed and savage.
explanation.walkthrough: Wild and fierce look like a pair of adjectives together, but only fierce is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent describes forceful, aggressive behaviour, which is what fierce means here.

clue.text: Fight waste?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a brawl or scuffle

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a question about whether fighting is pointless; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a scrap is a short brawl, and scrap metal or paper is leftover material thrown away.

clue.text: Get money from one in resale perhaps

indicators.note: in places the word for one inside the next word
perhaps marks the arrangement as only one possibility, so the letters may be reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Making cash from something by selling it on.
explanation.walkthrough: Resale fits the money theme so well that it seems part of the definition, but it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise an asset is to convert it into cash by selling it, the financial sense of the verb.

clue.text: Moss can't edit the paper

indicators.note: to edit text is to cut and rearrange it, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the two words taken letter by letter, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A man named Moss is not allowed to run the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Moss reads as a person and can't as an auxiliary; together they are just eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scotsman is an Edinburgh daily newspaper, so it is a paper in the press sense.

clue.text: Start of sprint on inferior track

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
of low quality

explanation.surface: An athlete begins a sprint on a bad running track.
explanation.walkthrough: Track looks like a running track; it is the trail left by an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the footprints or droppings a hunted animal leaves, the trail a tracker follows.

clue.text: Hindu instructor was wrecked on motorway

indicators.note: something wrecked is smashed up, so the word before it is broken and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the M1, Britain's first motorway, with its 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A Hindu teacher crashed on a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords read its digit as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher, a title of respect for a holy man who instructs disciples.

clue.text: Noted opening of sonnet?

parts.note: surface reading: a famous first line of a poem
setter's reading: made of musical notes, pointing to the interval spanning eight of them

explanation.surface: A well-known first line of a sonnet.
explanation.walkthrough: A Petrarchan sonnet opens with an eight-line group; the musical span of eight notes has the same name, hence noted.
explanation.definitionFit: The first eight lines of a Petrarchan sonnet form a unit with the same name as the eight-note interval.

clue.text: Cut, footnote about batting upsetting

indicators.note: to upset is to tip over, and in a down clue that turns the letters upside down
about means surrounding, so the word for footnote goes around what follows

parts.note: PS is a postscript, a note added at the foot of a letter
the side batting in cricket is in

explanation.surface: A footnote about a cricket innings that ruffles feathers has been cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is a small cut made with scissors, and as a verb it means to cut.

clue.text: Theatre work on senseless subject, perhaps

definitions.text: Theatre work on senseless subject, perhaps

parts.note: surface reading: a stage play about a meaningless topic
setter's reading: an anaesthetised patient in a hospital's surgical room

explanation.surface: A play staged about some pointless subject.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre is a hospital's operating theatre, and senseless means unconscious under anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery done in an operating theatre on an anaesthetised patient is what this word names.

clue.text: A title wrongly given

parts.note: taken as written
the form of address for an unmarried woman

explanation.surface: Someone has been addressed by the wrong honorific.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiss means astray or faultily, so something gone amiss has gone wrongly.

clue.text: Retired sailor has wrinkle with a bit of rigging

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the word for sailor is read backwards

parts.note: TAR is the old word for a seaman
a crease in the skin

explanation.surface: A pensioned-off seaman, wrinkled, with a piece of ship's tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: Retired looks like the sailor's age, matching the wrinkle, but it signals the backwards reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratlines are the small ropes tied across a ship's shrouds to form ladder rungs, part of the rigging.

clue.text: Lay claim to quiet rented building

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for soft

indicators.note: building means constructing, so these letters are put together in a new form

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone claims ownership of a peaceful leased property.
explanation.walkthrough: Rented building reads as a let house; building is the rearranging signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend to a throne or title is to assert a right to it, the old sense of laying claim.
